definition: TLS authenticates a server and encrypts communication between a client and server.
A certificate binds an identity to a public key using a digital signature.
A public key is the shareable half of an asymmetric key pair and can be included in a certificate.
A private key is the secret half of an asymmetric key pair that must be kept secure.
A certificate authority signs certificates that bind an identity to a public key.
A root certificate identifies a trusted authority at the top of a certificate chain.
A trust store is the collection of CA certificates a client accepts as trusted.
A PKI is the system of authorities, certificates, keys, and policies used to establish certificate trust.
DNS is the directory system that holds records for names in a domain.
A CNAME record points one DNS name to another and can carry ACM domain-control proof.
Domain validation proves that a certificate requester controls each requested domain name.
A hosted zone is a container of DNS records for a domain and its subdomains.
A wildcard certificate covers names at one subdomain level using an asterisk in the leftmost label.
A base domain is the domain name without a subdomain prefix.
HTTP is the web communication protocol used to retrieve the redirect-based validation proof.
An HTTP redirect sends a request for one URL to another URL.
An ARN identifies an AWS resource such as an ACM certificate.
Managed renewal is the ACM process for replacing eligible certificates before they expire.
A certificate chain lists issuing certificates in order so each certifies the one before it.
PEM is a text encoding used to represent certificates, chains, and keys.
A passphrase protects the private key returned by an ACM certificate export.
Reimport replaces an imported certificate while retaining its existing ARN and service associations.
ACME is a protocol that automates certificate issuance and lifecycle management between clients and certificate authorities.
An integrated service can use an ACM certificate directly for its endpoint.
